analysis:
MARKET REGIME: SPY is in a confirmed uptrend (+2.99% 20d SMA slope, price +1.1% above SMA50). Macro backdrop supports holding quality positions.

PORTFOLIO REVIEW: Six positions is one to three above the 3-5 target range. AMP (+15.2%), CI (+8.0%), WDAY (+6.6%), FDS (+7.0%), and A (+3.3%) are all working — thesis intact across each. The outlier is LII (-4.33%), which is the most concerning holding: this is the third LII trade in the journal, with the prior two both ending in stop hits (-6.63% and +4.82%). The pattern suggests persistent difficulty finding a clean entry. More critically, LII does NOT appear on today's screened candidate list, implying it may have softened technically or fundamentally since entry. Recommend watching LII closely — any break below $530 (approximately 1.5x ATR below current price) should trigger an exit. The position is small ($11,013) so the damage is contained, but holding a name that fails its own quality/trend screen three times is a thesis-break signal.

NEW TRADES: Capacity for new buys is only $13,058 — enough for one small position, but only if the setup is genuinely asymmetric. Several candidates are interesting (VEEV, ZBRA, BX), but all carry near-term disqualifiers: VEEV is extended +16.2% above SMA50 (chasing); BX has earnings in 9 days (binary event risk); ZBRA has earnings in 21 days and SMA50 acceleration that may be late-cycle. With 6 positions already open, $13K of headroom, and a historical profit factor of 0.08x, the evidence-based call is patience. A quiet cash book that protects the existing winners is the correct posture. No new buys are proposed this cycle.

SUMMARY: Hold AMP, CI, WDAY, FDS, A. Monitor LII with a firm stop near $530 and be prepared to close it. No new entries — cash preservation and current-winner protection is the value-add today. Revisit when LII resolves, headroom increases, or a candidate pulls back to a cleaner entry (e.g., VEEV near its SMA50 ~$169-175).
